## CEO BRIEFING

**For:** Dana Whitfield — board call 15:00 UTC
**As of:** 14:20 UTC, Monday 9 November 2026
**Incident:** INC-2026-1109-01 — **OPEN: mitigated, monitoring, root cause not established**

### State of play at 14:20

- **Mitigated at 12:58.** All Batch API traffic was cut over to the unaffected worker fleet; the affected fleet was drained and held out of rotation.
- **Error rate on the affected endpoint:** 0.4% within two minutes of the cutover (baseline 0.2%), holding 0.3–0.4% since; 0.3% at 14:12.
- **Verification window:** opened 13:00, closes 14:30. Incident policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before anything is declared resolved. **Earliest possible "resolved" is 14:30, and I will not call it before then.**
- **Root cause not established.** Two hypotheses remain live and neither has been tested; the rollback test has not been run.
- **Affected fleet is still out of service** and has not been returned to rotation.
- **Backlog re-drive** of jobs that failed during the window was ~60% complete at 13:52, with no failures on re-drive.

### What happened (all UTC, today)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 11:31 | Release `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` finishes rolling out to both fleets (three dependency bumps; database connection-pool max lowered 80 → 24 per worker) |
| 11:38 | Batch submission volume on fleet-a climbs to ~3x the morning average, driven by one customer's large scheduled job |
| 11:42 | **First alert.** `batch_api_5xx_rate` crosses threshold on fleet-a; 502s on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`. **Incident start** |
| 11:44 | Confirmed errors confined to fleet-a; fleet-b serving normally |
| 11:47 | Upstream object-storage provider ruled out (provider status green; Files API on the same provider healthy throughout) |
| 11:55 | First public status-page update |
| 12:03 | Correlation noted between the pool-ceiling change and workers queueing on database connections — **correlation, not tested** |
| 12:05 | Second status-page update (see caution below) |
| 12:31 | Decision not to roll back `r3` — rollback would destroy the evidence needed to test the hypothesis, and the same release is healthy on fleet-b. Mitigate by moving traffic instead |
| 12:58 | **Mitigation applied** — cutover complete, error rate on the floor within two minutes |
| 13:00 | Verification window opens (closes 14:30) |
| 13:20 | Error rate 0.3–0.4%, queue depth normal, no new customer reports |
| 13:52 | Failed-job re-drive ~60%, no failures on re-drive |
| 14:12 | Error rate 0.3%, 18 minutes remaining on the window |
| 14:20 | Current position: mitigated, monitoring |

### Cause — what we can and cannot say

Not established. Three positions:

- **Leading hypothesis:** the connection-pool ceiling cut in `r3` (80 → 24 per worker). It shipped 11 minutes before the first page and workers were observably queueing on database connections. **Against:** `r3` also went to fleet-b, which never degraded. **Untested — the rollback test has not been run.**
- **Secondary, still live:** concentrated load on fleet-a (~3x its morning average). **Against:** fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 3 November without elevated errors. **Untested.**
- **Rejected:** the upstream storage provider (ruled out at 11:47).

The first two may interact, but that is a third proposition and none of them has been tested.

### Who is hit

- **7 of the 9 accounts that use the Batch API** took failures, all on the same fleet. Seven of Northstar's 36 accounts overall.
- **Headline impact:** **17,602 of 58,900 Batch API requests failed between 11:42 and 12:58 — 29.9%.**
- Batch API was 58,900 of the 842,000 requests Northstar served across all API surfaces in that window (~7%).
- Failures by account: stark-industries 5,180 · contoso 3,410 · wayne-enterprises 2,790 · globex 2,240 · wonka-industries 2,020 · umbrella-health 1,560 · initech 402. The two other Batch accounts had zero failures.
- The other API surfaces (Inference, Embeddings, Files) are unrelated to this incident; the Files API was healthy throughout.

### Contoso and the SLA question

- Contoso is the **only affected account on a contract carrying service-level credits**. Two tickets today: 11:58 (failures) and 12:26 (asking where they stand on Schedule B credits, whether November breaches 99.9%, and what credit applies).
- **We cannot answer that today.** Under Schedule B §B.5, Monthly Availability is determined by Northstar from its own service records *after the end of the calendar month* and published within 10 business days of month end; a claim is due within 30 days of that publication. Commitment is 99.9%; credit tiers are 10% / 25% / 50%. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy.
- Their own reply to us (4 Nov, TKT-8841) says their retry-without-backoff fix is written but queued behind their Q4 freeze and not yet deployed. Context only — **do not raise this with them now.**
- I have replied to Contoso covering their status and their own figures (see customer email). Other affected accounts have open tickets with support; responses go out from Tomas against the cleared list only.

### If it comes up at the board — cleared to say, and nothing more

Cleared by Tomas and Ruth for use outside the company:

1. "There is an incident affecting the Batch API. It started at 11:42 UTC today."
2. "A mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering."
3. "We are monitoring before confirming recovery — we won't call it resolved until that's confirmed."
4. "A further update follows by 14:30 UTC."

**Do not say:**
- **Any cause.** None is established, and nothing has been tested.
- **Any recovery time.** No completion time has been given externally. (There is an internal planning estimate in the engineering channel; it is explicitly not for anyone outside that channel.)
- **Any impact numbers or fleet names.** Aggregate impact figures are not cleared for external use; per-account figures are cleared only for the affected customer, to that customer alone.

**Caution on the status page:** the 12:05 entry said we had "identified the cause" and expected full restoration within the hour. That was not accurate — Marcus instructed Ruth at 12:09 to stop publishing anything about cause. A correcting update goes out with this briefing; if a board member has seen the 12:05 entry, point them to the 14:20 update rather than defending the earlier wording.

**Confidential — internal only, do not raise at the board:** during triage Marcus found the batch worker's database role holds read *and* write access to the billing schema, which it has no reason to touch. It played no part in this incident. Standing over-permission; ticket **SEC-411** raised, Marcus owns it, target this week to narrow the role to read-only on the two tables it uses.

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**Handover from IC — INC-2026-1109-01, 14:20 UTC, 9 Nov 2026**
**Status: OPEN — mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.**
Nothing new assigned in this update; each strand continues with whoever already holds it.

### Position

- Mitigated 12:58 by cutting all Batch API traffic to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
- `POST /v1/batch/jobs` error rate: 0.4% at cutover (baseline 0.2%), 0.3–0.4% since, **0.3% at 14:12**. Queue depth on fleet-b normal. No new customer reports since cutover (13:20).
- **Verification window 13:00 → 14:30.** 90 minutes continuous normal error rate required before any resolution declaration. Nothing gets called resolved before 14:30, and only if the window closes clean.
- Re-drive of failed jobs was ~60% through affected accounts at 13:52, **no failures on re-drive** (Priya).

### Impact — computed from `customer-impact.csv` (window 11:42–12:58)

| Account | Fleet | Requests | Failures | First | Last |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stark-industries | fleet-a | 14,200 | 5,180 | 11:43 | 12:57 |
| contoso | fleet-a | 9,400 | 3,410 | 11:43 | 12:56 |
| wayne-enterprises | fleet-a | 7,850 | 2,790 | 11:44 | 12:57 |
| globex | fleet-a | 6,100 | 2,240 | 11:42 | 12:55 |
| wonka-industries | fleet-a | 5,900 | 2,020 | 11:46 | 12:57 |
| umbrella-health | fleet-a | 4,300 | 1,560 | 11:45 | 12:54 |
| initech | fleet-a | 1,150 | 402 | 11:51 | 12:48 |
| acme-corp | fleet-b | 6,700 | 0 | — | — |
| aperture-labs | fleet-b | 3,300 | 0 | — | — |
| **Total** | | **58,900** | **17,602** | | |

**Headline: 17,602 / 58,900 = 29.9% of Batch API requests failed in the window.** Batch was 58,900 of 842,000 platform-wide requests (~7%). 7 of 9 Batch accounts affected, all fleet-a. Fleet membership is internal and is not a reporting basis; the headline figure above is.

### Root cause — status of each position

- **H1 (leading, untested): connection-pool ceiling in `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3`**, max pool 80 → 24 per worker, shipped 11:31, eleven minutes before the first page; fleet-a workers observably queueing on DB connections (Marcus, 12:03). **Against:** `r3` shipped to fleet-b too and fleet-b never degraded. **The rollback test has not been run** — deliberately, per the 12:31 decision: rolling back removes the state on fleet-a needed to test it properly.
- **H2 (secondary, live, untested): concentrated load on fleet-a** — ~3x morning average from 11:38. **Against:** fleet-a absorbed a higher peak on 2026-11-03 without elevated errors.
- **H3 (rejected): upstream object-storage provider** — provider status green throughout, Files API on the same provider healthy. Ruled out 11:47.
- H1 × H2 interaction is a third proposition; **none of the three has been tested.** Do not describe any of these as identified or confirmed, internally or externally.

### Open at 14:20

1. Verification window closes 14:30 — resolution decision sits there, and only if it closes clean.
2. Rollback test of `r3` not run.
3. fleet-a still out of rotation, not returned to service.
4. Re-drive of failed jobs incomplete (~60% at 13:52).
5. Root cause not established.

### Customer / support queue (Tomas)

Open tickets today, all needing answers against the cleared list only:

- **TKT-8903 / TKT-8907 (contoso, 11:58 and 12:26)** — failures, then Schedule B credits. Replied 14:20 with their own figures and the §B.5 determination process; we cannot confirm a breach or a credit today.
- **TKT-8904 (umbrella-health, 12:11)** — compliance export due today. Their own figures are cleared for them: 4,300 requests, 1,560 failures, first 11:45, last 12:54.
- **TKT-8912 (wonka-industries, 12:44)** — asks whether to resubmit or whether we replay. Re-drive is in progress internally; **no commitment to replay is on the cleared list — needs clearance before it is stated to them.**
- **TKT-8918 (globex, 13:31)** — "are we affected?" Yes: 2,240 of 6,100 failed, first 11:42, last 12:55. Their own figures are cleared for them.
- **TKT-8841 (contoso, 4 Nov)** — their retry/no-backoff fix still undeployed (Q4 freeze). Context for any later Schedule B §B.2(b)/(c) exclusion discussion; **not to be raised with them now.**

### Communications state

- Status page: 11:55 *Investigating*, 12:05 *Identified*, **new 14:20 *Monitoring* update being published now**. The 12:05 entry wrongly claimed we had identified the cause; Marcus instructed Ruth at 12:09 to publish nothing further on cause. Ruth takes everything after 12:05 from Tomas' approved list.
- **Approved for external use, and this is the whole of it:**
  - that there is an incident affecting the Batch API, and when it started;
  - that a mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering;
  - that we are monitoring before confirming recovery;
  - that a further update will follow, with a stated time;
  - for a named customer writing to that customer only, that account's own impact figures.
- Not cleared externally: any cause, any aggregate impact figure, fleet names, re-drive commitments, or recovery times. The internal planning estimate for wrap-up lives in `#inc-batch-1109` and is not for anyone outside that channel — including executive briefings.

### Confidential

**SEC-411** (Marcus, target this week): batch worker's DB role holds read **and write** on the billing schema it has no reason to touch. Unrelated to this incident, no contributing role. Standing over-permission from review. Narrow to read-only on the two tables it uses. Northstar staff only — not for customers, status page, or any external channel.

## CUSTOM EMAIL

*(addressed to Contoso; sent as written)*

**To:** Contoso Ltd — via tickets TKT-8903 and TKT-8907
**Subject:** Re: Batch submits failing / Re: Batch submits failing - SLA — update from Northstar

Dear Contoso team,

Thank you for both tickets today — TKT-8903, raised at 11:58 UTC, and TKT-8907, raised at 12:26 UTC. This reply covers both.

**Incident status**

There is an incident affecting the Batch API, which started at 11:42 UTC today. We applied a mitigation at 12:58 UTC and the service is recovering. We are monitoring before confirming recovery. We will send you a further update by 14:30 UTC today.

**Your account's figures for the incident window (11:42–12:58 UTC)**

- Batch API requests made by Contoso: **9,400**
- Of those, requests that returned an error: **3,410** (approximately 36.3%)
- First failed request: **11:43 UTC**
- Last failed request: **12:56 UTC**

**On your service-level question (TKT-8907)**

We are not in a position to confirm today whether the 99.9% Monthly Availability commitment in Schedule B will be met for November, or which credit band would apply. As set out in section B.5 of Schedule B, Monthly Availability is determined by Northstar from its own service records after the end of the calendar month to which it relates, and published within 10 business days of month end. Any credit claim must be submitted within 30 days of that publication.

We will determine and publish the November figure under that process, and we will write to you again with a further update on the incident by 14:30 UTC today.

We are sorry for the disruption this has caused to your batch submissions.

Kind regards,
Northstar Support
on behalf of the Incident Commander, INC-2026-1109-01
